title: Chiropractic Manipulation
content: Chiropractic manipulation is most commonly applied to the spine but is also effective in improving mobility and alleviating pain in all joints throughout the body. Chiropractic manipulation is a safe non-invasive procedure that utilizes the doctor’s hands to mobilize a targeted joint. The manipulation uses a high-velocity, low-amplitude thrust over restricted joints. The cavitation (the “pop”) that may be heard is due to the release of gas (mostly nitrogen, oxygen, and carbon dioxide) in the joints.

title: Joints Chiropractic Manipulation Can Be Applied To
content: Manipulation can be applied to the following joints: Spine, Ears, Shoulder/clavicle, Elbow, Wrist, Hip, Knee/Ankle/foot, Ribs, Temporomandibular joint (TMJ).

title: Other Therapies
content: Using an integrative approach, Transcendence Health offers many alternative tools and techniques to meet your health and wellness needs.

title: Cupping
content: Cupping uses negative pressure to lift the muscle fibers and draw blood to the area to reduce stagnation and reduce pain and inflammation.

title: Graston (IASTM)
content: Evidence-based form of instrument-assisted soft tissue mobilization that enables clinicians to effectively break down scar tissue and fascial restrictions. Also known as muscle scraping, gua sha, or astym.

title: Manual Therapy
content: Hands-on approach to treat musculoskeletal pain and joint dysfunction. It involves kneading muscles and joint mobilization.

title: Therapeutic Exercise
content: Offers specific movement challenges that target the affected muscle group, joint complex and/or neurological pathways with the goal of correcting maladaptive patterns.

title: Kinesio Taping
content: Therapeutic taping technique that is used to relieve pain, reduce swelling and inflammation, and provide support to joints and muscles.

title: Dry Needling
content: Dry needling is a therapeutic technique used to treat musculoskeletal pain and dysfunction. Thin needles are inserted into a muscle’s trigger point to stimulate a healing response and alleviate pain.

title: Acupuncture
content: Acupuncture is a non-pharmacological, science-driven practice that is highly effective for people in all stages of life.

title: Does acupuncture really work?
content: Acupuncture is a 5000-year-old eastern medicine practice to help manage many conditions and diseases. Acupuncture has shown to be an effective treatment on its own or in conjunction with western medicine treatments.

title: How does acupuncture work?
content: The practice is based on achieving physical and psychological well-being through restoring balance. The goal of acupuncture is to move and balance qi (pronounced “chee”) in the body. The physician determines the specific pattern of imbalance causing the symptoms and gets to the root of the issue by inserting thin needles into the skin to stimulate the body’s natural healing abilities.

title: Are you not getting results from your primary care treatments?
content: If you are one of the many people looking for relief but not finding it from your primary care physician or from medication, you are an ideal candidate for acupuncture.

title: What can I expect during my treatment?
content: Treatments are relaxing, restorative, and virtually painless. When the needles are inserted, you may feel a pinch or pressure, coldness, and tingling. You will lie with the needles for 20-40 minutes, depending on the condition.

title: What can acupuncture treat?
content: While acupuncture excels at offering relief in treating numerous conditions, it also plays a large role in preventative health. Even if you have no active symptoms but want to remain that way, acupuncture is beneficial. Common conditions treated include smoking cessation, carpal tunnel, seasonal allergies and sinusitis, neuro conditions such as Bell’s Palsy, Parkinson’s, MS, AS, and neuropathy, migraines and headaches, low back pain, plantar fasciitis, loss of smell or taste post COVID, dry eyes, PMS and dysmenorrhea, infertility, fatigue, vertigo, and frozen shoulder.
